title: Touch floors are hardcoded in 4 places; the pure rules module is not the single source the UI consumes
evidence:
touch_targets.gd defines the rule and a helper:
  const MIN_TOUCH_PRIMARY := 160
  const MIN_TOUCH_SECONDARY := 120
  static func ensure_min_touch(rect: Vector2, role: int) -> Vector2:
	var min_size := min_touch_size(role)
	return Vector2(maxf(rect.x, min_size), maxf(rect.y, min_size))

street_theme.tres mirrors it (read by NO prod code, only the test's get_constant):
  Button/constants/min_touch_size = 160
  Button/constants/min_touch_size_secondary = 120

The actual UI hardcodes its own copies:
  street.tscn:211 (DominantButton): custom_minimum_size = Vector2(160, 200)
  street.gd:607 (_make_big_button): button.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(120, 150)

Repo grep proves ensure_min_touch / MIN_TOUCH_PRIMARY / MIN_TOUCH_SECONDARY / get_constant("min_touch_size" appear ONLY in touch_targets.gd (self-refs) and test_economy.gd — never in any production scene or script.
detail: The pure module exposes ensure_min_touch() but no UI code calls it; floors are hardcoded separately in the scene, _make_big_button, and a mirror-only theme constant. A floor change needs 4 edits — the PR's 'one-line constant change' promise breaks.
recommended_fix: Have _make_big_button and DominantButton derive custom_minimum_size from FinLitTouchTargets.MIN_TOUCH_* (or ensure_min_touch); delete the unread theme constant. One source, no drift.
